# Purpose

This file scores the nine completed one-year-ahead rolling-origin forecasts from 2017-2025.

For each target year, municipality rankings are constructed using information available before that year and evaluated against the following year's observed chikungunya cases and deaths.

Three rules are compared at identical coverage:

1. Rolling-origin INLA forecast ranking.
2. Age-only ranking using the previous year's proportion aged 65+.
3. Naive ranking using the previous year's reported chikungunya cases.

The primary performance measure is the share of observed target-year cases or deaths captured by the top one-third of municipalities.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = TRUE, message = TRUE)

source("00_setup.R")

STUDY_START <- 2016L
STUDY_END <- 2025L
TARGET_YEARS <- 2017:2025
EXPECTED_N_MUNI <- 5570L
TOP_N <- ceiling(EXPECTED_N_MUNI / 3)

results_dir <- RESULTS_DIR
pred_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "rolling_origin", "predictions")
score_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "rolling_origin", "scoring")

dir.create(score_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

cat("Target years:", paste(TARGET_YEARS, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Matched top-third municipality count:", TOP_N, "\n")
```

# 1. Load completed inputs

```{r load-inputs}
if (!exists("pop_panel_age")) {
  if (!file.exists(result_path("pop_panel_age.rds"))) {
    stop("pop_panel_age.rds not found in RESULTS_DIR: ", RESULTS_DIR)
  }
  pop_panel_age <- readRDS(result_path("pop_panel_age.rds"))
}

if (!exists("Chik_total")) {
  stop(
    "Chik_total is not in memory. Run the revised 01_data_import_cleaning.Rmd first, ",
    "then run this scoring file."
  )
}

stopifnot(
  n_distinct(pop_panel_age$code_muni) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI
)

pred_files <- file.path(
  pred_dir,
  sprintf("forecast_annual_predict_%d.csv", TARGET_YEARS)
)

missing_pred <- pred_files[!file.exists(pred_files)]

if (length(missing_pred) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing rolling-origin prediction files:\n",
    paste(missing_pred, collapse = "\n")
  )
}

cat("All 9 prediction files found.\n")
```

# 2. Standardize municipality IDs and build observed annual outcomes

`Chik_total` is already the confirmed 2016-2025 analytic dataset. Observed outcomes are aggregated by municipality and notification year.

```{r observed-outcomes}
observed_annual <- Chik_total %>%
  mutate(
    code_muni = stringr::str_pad(
      substr(as.character(ID_MUNICIP), 1, 6),
      width = 6,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    ),
    year = lubridate::year(as.Date(DT_SIN_PRI)),
    death = as.integer(as.character(EVOLUCAO) == "2")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13),
    year %in% STUDY_START:STUDY_END,
    !is.na(code_muni)
  ) %>%
  group_by(code_muni, year) %>%
  summarise(
    cases = n(),
    deaths = sum(death, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

muni_universe <- pop_panel_age %>%
  transmute(
    code_muni = stringr::str_pad(
      substr(as.character(code_muni), 1, 6),
      width = 6,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    )
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(code_muni)

stopifnot(nrow(muni_universe) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI)

annual_grid <- tidyr::crossing(
  code_muni = muni_universe$code_muni,
  year = STUDY_START:STUDY_END
) %>%
  left_join(observed_annual, by = c("code_muni", "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    cases = replace_na(cases, 0L),
    deaths = replace_na(deaths, 0L)
  )

cat("Observed annual grid rows:", nrow(annual_grid), "\n")
cat("Observed cases 2016-2025:", sum(annual_grid$cases), "\n")
cat("Observed deaths 2016-2025:", sum(annual_grid$deaths), "\n")
```

# 3. Build the age-only baseline using past-only information

For target year `t`, the age-only rule uses the proportion aged 65+ in year `t-1`.

```{r age-only}
age65_by_year <- pop_panel_age %>%
  mutate(
    code_muni = stringr::str_pad(
      substr(as.character(code_muni), 1, 6),
      width = 6,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(year %in% STUDY_START:(STUDY_END - 1L)) %>%
  group_by(code_muni, year) %>%
  summarise(
    total_pop = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_65plus = sum(pop[age >= 65], na.rm = TRUE),
    prop_65plus = pop_65plus / total_pop,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(
  n_distinct(age65_by_year$code_muni) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
  sum(!is.finite(age65_by_year$prop_65plus)) == 0L
)
```

# 4. Read and validate the nine rolling-origin forecasts

```{r load-forecasts}
forecast_all <- purrr::map_dfr(
  TARGET_YEARS,
  function(yy) {
    f <- file.path(
      pred_dir,
      sprintf("forecast_annual_predict_%d.csv", yy)
    )

    x <- readr::read_csv(
      f,
      show_col_types = FALSE,
      col_types = cols(
        code_muni = col_character(),
        .default = col_guess()
      )
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        code_muni = stringr::str_pad(
          substr(as.character(code_muni), 1, 6),
          width = 6,
          side = "left",
          pad = "0"
        ),
        target_year = as.integer(target_year)
      )

    required_cols <- c(
      "code_muni",
      "target_year",
      "forecast_annual"
    )

    if (!all(required_cols %in% names(x))) {
      stop(
        "Missing required columns in ",
        basename(f),
        ": ",
        paste(setdiff(required_cols, names(x)), collapse = ", ")
      )
    }

    if (nrow(x) != EXPECTED_N_MUNI) {
      stop(
        basename(f),
        " has ",
        nrow(x),
        " rows; expected ",
        EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
        "."
      )
    }

    if (n_distinct(x$code_muni) != EXPECTED_N_MUNI) {
      stop("Duplicate or missing municipalities in ", basename(f), ".")
    }

    if (!all(x$target_year == yy)) {
      stop("target_year mismatch in ", basename(f), ".")
    }

    if (any(!is.finite(x$forecast_annual))) {
      stop("Non-finite forecast_annual values in ", basename(f), ".")
    }

    x %>%
      select(code_muni, target_year, forecast_annual)
  }
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(forecast_all) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI * length(TARGET_YEARS),
  n_distinct(forecast_all$target_year) == length(TARGET_YEARS)
)

print(
  forecast_all %>%
    count(target_year, name = "n_municipalities")
)
```

# 5. Assemble a past-only evaluation dataset for each target year

For each target year:

- `forecast_annual` is the model forecast generated without observing the target year.
- `last_year_cases` is the prior year's observed case count.
- `prop_65plus` is the prior year's population proportion aged 65+.
- `actual_cases` and `actual_deaths` are used only for evaluation.

```{r evaluation-dataset}
evaluation_data <- purrr::map_dfr(
  TARGET_YEARS,
  function(yy) {

    forecast_y <- forecast_all %>%
      filter(target_year == yy)

    actual_y <- annual_grid %>%
      filter(year == yy) %>%
      transmute(
        code_muni,
        actual_cases = cases,
        actual_deaths = deaths
      )

    last_year_y <- annual_grid %>%
      filter(year == yy - 1L) %>%
      transmute(
        code_muni,
        last_year_cases = cases
      )

    age_y <- age65_by_year %>%
      filter(year == yy - 1L) %>%
      transmute(
        code_muni,
        prop_65plus
      )

    out <- muni_universe %>%
      left_join(forecast_y, by = "code_muni") %>%
      left_join(last_year_y, by = "code_muni") %>%
      left_join(age_y, by = "code_muni") %>%
      left_join(actual_y, by = "code_muni") %>%
      mutate(
        target_year = yy,
        last_year_cases = replace_na(last_year_cases, 0L),
        actual_cases = replace_na(actual_cases, 0L),
        actual_deaths = replace_na(actual_deaths, 0L)
      )

    stopifnot(
      nrow(out) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
      sum(is.na(out$forecast_annual)) == 0L,
      sum(is.na(out$prop_65plus)) == 0L,
      sum(is.na(out$actual_cases)) == 0L,
      sum(is.na(out$actual_deaths)) == 0L
    )

    out
  }
)

cat("Evaluation rows:", nrow(evaluation_data), "\n")
```

# 6. Score matched top-third capture

Exactly `TOP_N` municipalities are selected for every rule and target year.

Ties are broken deterministically by municipality code so that each rule always selects the same number of municipalities.

```{r score-functions}
capture_top_n <- function(df, rank_col, outcome_col, n_select = TOP_N) {

  total_outcome <- sum(df[[outcome_col]], na.rm = TRUE)

  if (total_outcome <= 0) {
    return(
      tibble(
        captured = NA_real_,
        total = total_outcome,
        capture_share = NA_real_
      )
    )
  }

  selected <- df %>%
    arrange(
      desc(.data[[rank_col]]),
      code_muni
    ) %>%
    slice_head(n = n_select)

  tibble(
    captured = sum(selected[[outcome_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
    total = total_outcome,
    capture_share = captured / total
  )
}

rule_spec <- tibble(
  rule = c(
    "Rolling-origin forecast",
    "Age-only",
    "Last-year cases"
  ),
  rank_col = c(
    "forecast_annual",
    "prop_65plus",
    "last_year_cases"
  )
)

score_one_year <- function(df_year) {

  yy <- unique(df_year$target_year)

  purrr::pmap_dfr(
    rule_spec,
    function(rule, rank_col) {

      cases_score <- capture_top_n(
        df_year,
        rank_col = rank_col,
        outcome_col = "actual_cases"
      )

      deaths_score <- capture_top_n(
        df_year,
        rank_col = rank_col,
        outcome_col = "actual_deaths"
      )

      tibble(
        target_year = yy,
        rule = rule,
        n_selected = TOP_N,
        cases_captured = cases_score$captured,
        cases_total = cases_score$total,
        cases_capture_share = cases_score$capture_share,
        deaths_captured = deaths_score$captured,
        deaths_total = deaths_score$total,
        deaths_capture_share = deaths_score$capture_share
      )
    }
  )
}
```

```{r yearly-scoring}
yearly_performance <- evaluation_data %>%
  group_split(target_year) %>%
  purrr::map_dfr(score_one_year) %>%
  arrange(target_year, factor(
    rule,
    levels = c(
      "Rolling-origin forecast",
      "Age-only",
      "Last-year cases"
    )
  ))

print(yearly_performance, n = Inf)
```

# 7. Summarize performance across the nine held-out years

The median is the primary cross-year summary. Interquartile range and full range are retained to show year-to-year variability.

```{r summary-performance}
performance_summary <- yearly_performance %>%
  group_by(rule) %>%
  summarise(
    n_years = n(),
    median_cases_capture = median(cases_capture_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25_cases_capture = quantile(cases_capture_share, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75_cases_capture = quantile(cases_capture_share, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_cases_capture = min(cases_capture_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_cases_capture = max(cases_capture_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_deaths_capture = median(deaths_capture_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25_deaths_capture = quantile(deaths_capture_share, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75_deaths_capture = quantile(deaths_capture_share, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_deaths_capture = min(deaths_capture_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_deaths_capture = max(deaths_capture_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(performance_summary)
```

# 8. Main rolling-origin performance figure

Each point is a genuinely held-out target year. The dashed horizontal line marks the 33.3% expected share under a random one-third selection, shown only as a visual reference rather than as an additional fitted baseline.

```{r figure-data}
plot_data <- yearly_performance %>%
  select(
    target_year,
    rule,
    cases_capture_share,
    deaths_capture_share
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      cases_capture_share,
      deaths_capture_share
    ),
    names_to = "outcome",
    values_to = "capture_share"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = recode(
      outcome,
      cases_capture_share = "Observed cases captured",
      deaths_capture_share = "Observed deaths captured"
    ),
    rule = factor(
      rule,
      levels = c(
        "Rolling-origin forecast",
        "Age-only",
        "Last-year cases"
      )
    )
  )
```

```{r main-figure, fig.width=9.2, fig.height=4.4}
# Final Figure 6 design used for the manuscript Results.
rule_colors <- c(
  "Rolling-origin forecast" = "#0072B2",
  "Last-year cases" = "#D55E00",
  "Age-only" = "#009E73"
)

rule_shapes <- c(
  "Rolling-origin forecast" = 16,
  "Last-year cases" = 15,
  "Age-only" = 17
)

plot_data <- yearly_performance %>%
  select(target_year, rule, cases_capture_share, deaths_capture_share) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(cases_capture_share, deaths_capture_share),
    names_to = "outcome",
    values_to = "capture_share"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = recode(
      outcome,
      cases_capture_share = "Reported cases",
      deaths_capture_share = "Reported deaths"
    ),
    rule = factor(
      rule,
      levels = c("Rolling-origin forecast", "Last-year cases", "Age-only")
    )
  )

make_capture_panel <- function(data, outcome_label) {
  data %>%
    filter(outcome == outcome_label) %>%
    ggplot(
      aes(
        x = target_year,
        y = capture_share,
        color = rule,
        shape = rule,
        group = rule
      )
    ) +
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = TOP_N / EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
      linewidth = 0.5,
      linetype = "dotted"
    ) +
    geom_line(aes(linewidth = rule)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.6) +
    scale_color_manual(values = rule_colors) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = rule_shapes) +
    scale_linewidth_manual(
      values = c(
        "Rolling-origin forecast" = 1.05,
        "Last-year cases" = 0.85,
        "Age-only" = 0.85
      ),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = TARGET_YEARS) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
      breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1),
      limits = c(0, 1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.015))
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Target year",
      y = "Share captured",
      title = outcome_label,
      color = NULL,
      shape = NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 9.5),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}

p_cases <- make_capture_panel(plot_data, "Reported cases")
p_deaths <- make_capture_panel(plot_data, "Reported deaths")

rolling_origin_figure <- p_cases | p_deaths
rolling_origin_figure <- rolling_origin_figure +
  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.8, "lines"),
    plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13)
  )

rolling_origin_figure
```

# Interpretation guardrails

- Each rolling-origin forecast is evaluated only against a year that was not used as an observed response in that fold.
- The age-only and last-year-case baselines use only information available before the target year.
- Capture shares are descriptive held-out performance measures; they are not estimates of vaccine effectiveness or prevented cases/deaths.
- The dotted 33.3% line is a visual reference for equal random coverage, not a fourth fitted comparison rule.
- This file scores the primary one-year-ahead rolling-origin analysis only. The longer-horizon 2016-2022 to 2024-2025 analysis and the 2026 external validation remain separate analyses.

```{r}
# ============================================================

make_main <- function(outcome_name, panel_tag, y_label) {

  main_long %>%
    filter(outcome == outcome_name) %>%
    ggplot(aes(
      x = target_year,
      y = capture_share,
      color = rule,
      group = rule
    )) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = cols,
      breaks = names(cols),
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2017:2025) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 1),
      breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
      labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = y_label,
      tag = panel_tag
    ) +
    theme_fig6 +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    )
}

p_main_cases <- make_main(
  "cases_capture_share",
  "a",
  "Share of cases captured"
)

p_main_deaths <- make_main(
  "deaths_capture_share",
  "b",
  "Share of deaths captured"
)

# ============================================================
# 3. Forecast advantage in percentage points
# ============================================================

delta_data <- main_long %>%
  filter(
    rule %in% c(
      "Rolling-origin forecast",
      "Last-year cases"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(rule = as.character(rule)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = rule,
    values_from = capture_share
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_pp = 100 * (
      `Rolling-origin forecast` -
      `Last-year cases`
    ),
    direction = if_else(
      delta_pp >= 0,
      "Forecast higher",
      "Last-year higher"
    )
  )

make_delta <- function(outcome_name) {

  delta_data %>%
    filter(outcome == outcome_name) %>%
    ggplot(aes(
      x = target_year,
      y = delta_pp,
      fill = direction
    )) +
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "grey50",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ) +
    geom_col(width = 0.65) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Forecast higher" = "#2477B4",
        "Last-year higher" = "#E47D39"
      ),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2017:2025) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(-12, 12),
      breaks = c(-10, -5, 0, 5, 10),
      labels = function(x) {
        ifelse(x > 0, paste0("+", x), as.character(x))
      }
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Target year",
      y = "Forecast − last-year difference"
    ) +
    theme_fig6
}

p_delta_cases <- make_delta("cases_capture_share")
p_delta_deaths <- make_delta("deaths_capture_share")

# ============================================================
# 4. Final Figure 6
# ============================================================

fig6_improved <- (
  (p_main_cases | p_main_deaths) /
  (p_delta_cases | p_delta_deaths)
) +
  plot_layout(
    heights = c(1.65, 1),
    guides = "collect"
  ) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(fig6_improved)


```




# Interpretation guardrails

- Each rolling-origin forecast is evaluated only against a year that was not used as an observed response in that fold.
- The age-only and last-year-case baselines use only information available before the target year.
- Capture shares are descriptive held-out performance measures; they are not estimates of vaccine effectiveness or prevented cases/deaths.
- The dotted 33.3% line is a visual reference for equal random coverage, not a fourth fitted comparison rule.
- This file scores the primary one-year-ahead rolling-origin analysis only. The longer-horizon 2016-2022 to 2024-2025 analysis and the 2026 external validation remain separate analyses.
